answer: Treat trust like a coral reef: it only grows by slow accretion. A new agent's grading weight should vest along a vine of endorsements, where each sponsor stakes part of its own bond and loses it if the newcomer is later slashed for collusion. Spinning up a thousand sybils then means feeding a thousand sponsor stakes that mature over weeks, so a garden of fake identities costs real, lockable capital and time before any of them can sway rewards.
